subject: E2E p95/p99 targets + streaming throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@vitalityops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: E2E p95/p99 targets + streaming throughput clarifications

Hi Elaine / Vitality SRE team — thanks again for the call yesterday. Quick recap and a short list of asks so we can scope a short hosted-vs-incumbent comparison POC.

High-level acceptance targets you mentioned on the call (please confirm):
- End-to-end p95 (user-perceived from app -> model -> app): <= 200 ms
- End-to-end p99: <= 450 ms
- Sustained traffic envelope: 120 requests/sec (burst to 250 rps for 5m windows)
- Concurrency target for interactive streaming: 40 concurrent streaming sessions with avg token throughput ~18 tokens/sec/session

Concrete asks from Redwood to validate fitment:
1) Can you share 24h tail traces (p95/p99) from your current provider for both standard generation and streaming endpoints? Ideally sample request/response timing and token-stream deltas.
2) Any client-side shard/edge-proxy time (ms) we should include in the E2E numbers?
3) Are there specific request shapes we should prioritize (prompt length, response token count)? On the call you mentioned 120-200 input tokens and 80-160 output tokens as common cases — confirm.
4) Preferred test window(s) next week for a 2-hour live comparison (we'll coordinate traffic replay + hosted config).

Next steps proposed (Redwood):
- Ben to schedule a short infra sync to confirm test endpoints and keys.
- Marissa to propose a baseline hosted config (model variant + concurrency + prefix caching on) and expected per-token tail.
- Michael (me) to accept traces and align on success criteria + runbook.

Attachments: call-recording-20260903.mp4 (post-call recording), request-sample-examples.txt (small), vitality-trace-sample-request (placeholder).

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight. If the p99 gap is within ~2x of your incumbent we can propose an optimization plan (quant + routing) before committing to dedicated capacity.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@vitalityops.com>

On Fri, Sep 4, 2026 at 09:12 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elaine / Vitality SRE team — thanks again for the call yesterday. Quick recap and a short list of asks so we can scope a short hosted-vs-incumbent comparison POC.
> 
> High-level acceptance targets you mentioned on the call (please confirm):
> - End-to-end p95 (user-perceived from app -> model -> app): <= 200 ms
> - End-to-end p99: <= 450 ms
> - Sustained traffic envelope: 120 requests/sec (burst to 250 rps for 5m windows)
> - Concurrency target for interactive streaming: 40 concurrent streaming sessions with avg token throughput ~18 tokens/sec/session

Thanks Michael — that summary matches what we discussed with one correction on bursts: our legal traffic model allows bursts up to 300 rps but only 2x/day and those are shaped by the edge.

Answers inline: 
1) We attached a 24h sample (vitality-trace-samples.zip) with request/response timestamps and split by endpoint (standard vs streaming). These are scrubbed for PHI.
2) Edge/ELB adds ~12-20 ms median, ~40-70 ms tail depending on region. We call that out separately in the traces.
3) Confirmed: 120-200 input tokens, 80-160 output tokens are the most common. Also include long-response outliers ~400 tokens (rare).
4) We can do a live comparison on Tue 2026-09-08 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2026-09-10 13:00-15:00 PT. Prefer Tue if you can.

Quick notes on current provider: their p95 for standard generation is ~180ms, p99 ~420ms (includes edge). For streaming the p95 is ~220ms (first token), p99 ~700ms when measured end-to-end for sessions with lots of context. Those streaming p99 numbers are our primary pain point.

We'll send the traces via the s3 link listed below and attach a small sample set directly to email. Also included a short topo diagram for our edge (attached).

Elaine
SRE Lead, VitalityOps

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine.cho@vitalityops.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: E2E p95/p99 targets + streaming throughput clarifications

Thanks Elaine — really helpful. Proposed test plan below (keeps the runbook minimal):

Test plan (2-hour window, Tue 2026-09-08 09:00-11:00 PT):
- 09:00-09:15: warmup (traffic replay at 10% volume to prime caches, capture baseline)
- 09:15-10:30: main compare (2x 30min steady-state runs at target envelope: 120 rps sustained + 2x 5m bursts to 250 rps)
- 10:30-10:50: streaming stress (ramp to 40 concurrent streaming sessions, vary prompt length)
- 10:50-11:00: cool-down and logs collection

Success criteria (quick):
- For standard generation: hosted p95 <= incumbent p95 + 30 ms, hosted p99 <= incumbent p99 * 1.5 and <= 700 ms absolute
- For streaming: first-token p95 <= incumbent first-token p95 + 50 ms; overall streaming session p99 <= incumbent p99 * 1.8 (we want to see measurable tail improvements or clear optimization path)

Data we'll need from Vitality before the run:
- The 24h trace bundle (you mentioned s3 link) and two example request payloads for replay
- Short allowlist of client IPs or an ephemeral test key to call your edge if you prefer replay post-edge

Marissa — can you confirm the hosted baseline config you intend to run (model + concurrency + streaming chunk size + kv cache on/off)? Also add an estimate of expected per-token cost for the test so the customer can evaluate unit economics during the session.

If Tue works for Vitality, we'll lock the window and send a detailed runbook + monitoring dashboard link.

-Ben
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

A few operational clarifications:
- We'll provision an ephemeral test key and IP allowlist for Redwood — expect it in a separate email from our security mailbox later today.

Attachments: vitality-trace-samples.zip (scrubbed), edge-topology.pdf (diagram).

Looking forward to the run. If you can share the runbook and the dashboard link by EOD Monday that would be ideal so our on-call can review.

Elaine Cho
